draft.title: Government economic objectives
card: An economic objective is a goal a government sets for how the economy should perform. Most Australian governments share a few main ones.
Growth
steady growth in the goods and services the economy produces. Steady means growth that is not wildly up and down.
Jobs and prices
low unemployment, so most people who want work can find it, and low, stable inflation, so prices rise only slowly and predictably.
Fairness
a fair share of income, so the gap between richer and poorer households does not grow too wide.
draft.remember: Governments aim for steady growth, low unemployment, low stable inflation and a fair share of income.

a.q: Which goal is an economic objective of a government?
opts: Low unemployment, so most people who want work can find it
Zero inflation, so prices never change at all
Equal incomes for every household in the country
The fastest possible growth in any single year
a.why: Low unemployment is one of the main objectives. The other options are extreme versions: the objective is low and stable inflation, a fair share of income rather than equal incomes, and steady growth rather than the fastest possible.
a.clue: The card uses words like low, steady and fair, not extremes.

b.q: Prices in Tamara's town rose 12% one year, then 1% the next, then 9% the year after. Which objective is the government failing to meet?
opts: Low and stable inflation
Steady economic growth
A fair share of income
Low unemployment
b.why: The rise in prices is inflation, and it jumps up and down, so it is neither low nor stable. The facts say nothing about output, jobs or how income is shared, so the other objectives cannot be judged from them.
b.clue: Look at what is happening to prices, and whether the changes are steady.

a.best: Low unemployment, so most people who want work can find it

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and repeats the card's wording word for word ('so most people who want work can find it'). A student could pick it by matching text without understanding the idea.

Inflation is measured across the whole economy (the CPI), not for one town. Framing the scenario as prices in 'Tamara's town' suggests governments target local price changes. Saying 'prices in Australia' would be accurate.

a.q: A treasurer wants a goal that matches the government's usual economic objectives. Which goal fits?
opts: Keep unemployment low across the economy
Hold inflation at zero so prices never change
Make every household's income exactly equal
Push growth as fast as possible every year
a.why: Low unemployment is one of the main objectives. The others are extreme versions: the objective is low and stable inflation, not zero, a fair share of income rather than equal incomes, and steady growth rather than the fastest possible.
a.clue: The objectives use words like low, steady and fair, not extremes.
